Norman Blinds and Shades Now Available at Sound View Window & Door

Norman Blinds and Shades Now Available at Sound View Window & Door: Your Guide to Custom, Energy-Efficient Window Treatments in Seattle

Norman Blinds and Shades are now available at Sound View Window & Door, offering a perfect blend of style, functionality, and energy efficiency for your home. These custom window treatments are designed to enhance the aesthetic appeal of your living spaces while providing practical benefits such as improved insulation and light control. In this article, we will explore the key features and benefits of Norman Blinds and Shades, installation options, and how they can transform your home environment. Whether you're looking to upgrade your current window treatments or are in the process of a home renovation, this guide will provide valuable insights into why Norman Blinds and Shades are an excellent choice for homeowners in Seattle.

Key Features

Norman Blinds and Shades come with several standout features that make them a popular choice among homeowners.

  1. Custom Solutions: Each product can be tailored to fit your specific window dimensions and design preferences, ensuring a perfect fit and look.
  2. Energy Efficiency Benefits: These window treatments are designed to help regulate indoor temperatures, reducing reliance on heating and cooling systems.
  3. Variety of Materials Offered: Customers can choose from a wide range of materials, including fabric, wood, and synthetic options, allowing for personalized style and functionality.

These features not only enhance the visual appeal of your home but also contribute to energy savings and comfort.

Benefits

Using Norman Blinds and Shades offers numerous advantages that can significantly improve your living environment.

  1. Cost Savings on Energy Bills: By providing better insulation, these window treatments can help lower your energy costs throughout the year.
  2. Enhanced Comfort in Homes: The ability to control light and heat contributes to a more comfortable indoor atmosphere, making your home more enjoyable.
  3. Aesthetic Appeal and Sustainability: With a variety of styles and materials, Norman Blinds and Shades can complement any interior design while being environmentally friendly.

These benefits make Norman Blinds and Shades a smart investment for homeowners looking to enhance their living spaces.

Installation Options

When it comes to installation, Sound View Window & Door offers professional services to ensure a seamless experience from consultation to installation.

  1. Professional Installation Services Offered: Expert installers will handle the entire process, ensuring that your blinds and shades are fitted correctly and function optimally.
  2. Seamless Experience from Consultation to Installation: The team will guide you through the selection process, helping you choose the best options for your home.
  3. Post-Installation Support: After installation, you can rely on Sound View Window & Door for any adjustments or maintenance needed to keep your window treatments in top condition.

This level of service ensures that you receive not only high-quality products but also a hassle-free installation experience.

What Are the Key Features of Norman Blinds and Shades Offered at Sound View Window & Door?

Norman Blinds and Shades are designed with several key features that set them apart from other window treatments.

  • Custom Solutions: Tailored to fit your windows perfectly.
  • Energy Efficiency: Helps maintain indoor temperatures and reduce energy costs.
  • Material Variety: Options include fabric, wood, and synthetic materials for personalized style.

How Do Custom Window Shades Enhance Your Home's Style and Functionality?

Custom window shades enhance your home by providing a tailored look that complements your interior design. They also offer functionality through light control and insulation, making your living spaces more comfortable and energy-efficient.

What Energy-Efficient Materials and Motorized Options Are Available?

Norman Blinds and Shades are available in energy-efficient materials that help reduce heat loss in winter and keep your home cool in summer. Additionally, motorized options allow for convenient operation, making it easy to adjust your shades with the touch of a button.

How Can You Benefit from Professional Installation and Window Replacement Services in Seattle?

Professional installation ensures that your window treatments are fitted correctly, maximizing their effectiveness and lifespan. Sound View Window & Door provides expert installation services, making the process easy and stress-free for homeowners.

What Is the Process for Measuring and Installing Norman Blinds and Shades?

The process begins with a consultation where experts measure your windows to ensure a perfect fit. After selecting your desired styles and materials, the installation team will schedule a time to install your new blinds and shades, ensuring everything is done to your satisfaction.

How Does Sound View Window & Door Offer Free Estimates and Showroom Visits?

Sound View Window & Door provides free estimates to help you understand the costs involved before making a decision. Additionally, you can visit their showroom to see the various options available and get a feel for how they will look in your home.

Why Are Norman Blinds and Shades the Best Choice for Privacy and Energy Savings?

Norman Blinds and Shades offer excellent privacy control while also being designed to enhance energy efficiency. Their ability to block out light and insulate windows makes them a top choice for homeowners looking to save on energy costs while maintaining privacy.

What Makes Norman Blinds Superior for Privacy Compared to Other Window Treatments?

Norman Blinds are designed with materials that effectively block visibility from the outside while allowing natural light to filter in. This unique combination provides privacy without sacrificing brightness in your home.

How Do Energy-Efficient Window Treatments Reduce Utility Costs?

Energy-efficient window treatments like Norman Blinds and Shades help reduce utility costs by minimizing heat transfer through windows. This means your heating and cooling systems work less, leading to lower energy bills.

What Do Seattle Customers Say About Their Experience with Norman Blinds at Sound View Window & Door?

Customers in Seattle have praised the quality and aesthetic appeal of Norman Blinds and Shades, noting significant improvements in energy efficiency and comfort in their homes. Many appreciate the professional installation services provided by Sound View Window & Door.

Which Case Studies Highlight Successful Window Replacement and Blind Installation?

Several case studies demonstrate the effectiveness of Norman Blinds and Shades in various Seattle homes, showcasing how these window treatments have improved energy efficiency and enhanced interior design.

How Do Customer Reviews Reflect Quality and Service Excellence?

Customer reviews consistently highlight the quality of Norman Blinds and Shades, as well as the exceptional service provided by Sound View Window & Door. Many customers report satisfaction with both the products and the installation process.

Milgard Essence French Style Sliding Glass Doors Recently Installed in Seattle

(Update:  Milgard has discontinued the Essence product line) Recently, our installation crew installed a new Milgard Essence french style sliding patio door to replace a window in this Seattle, WA home.  See the photos below.  The project involved enlarging the opening in the existing wall, removing the existing window and adding a new 4 x 8 header.  The exterior was wrapped on the exterior with 5/4 x 4 cedar and the interior was trimmed with new 9/16" x 2 1/2" chair rail. The new patio door is from Milgard's Essence Series and features a VG fir interior and white "Frost" fiberglass exterior.  The hardware is a brushed chrome finish. Comments from the homeowner: "We purchased a Milgard sliding patio door through Sound View and had it installed by them as well. Had an excellent experience from start to finish. The door was ordered and arrived on time, and installation was completed in 1.5 days! (This included cutting a new hole in our house). Our installation team did an excellent job and went above and beyond to minimize any finishing work needed, and kept the jobsite extremely clean. We will definitely go to Sound View again for any window or door needs on our house." item.title: Corvid-19 Procedures
item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com
item.content:encoded:
Dear Sound View current & potential clients,
We are reaching out to inform you that during the current COVID-19 situation we remain committed to offering our same high level of customer service, while at the same time being as socially responsible as possible. In the interest of the health and safety of our staff and customers, we have implemented special procedures to reduce the potential exposure.
Quotes & Critical Measurements 1) During this time, our field reps will not be entering the home for quoting purposes. They will take approximate measurements from the exterior only. We ask that you email photos of the interior if needed to put together the proposal. 2) Virtual jobsite tours are available using zoom.com. 3) When direct meetings are necessary, our field reps will be practicing 6’ social distancing, and avoiding direct contact with individuals and surfaces. 4) Documents that require customer signatures will be sent & received electronically whenever possible. 5) If there is an at-risk person at the property, we ask that they be kept isolated from our employees for the safety of everyone
Installations 1) We ask that, if possible, clients be out of the building or in a separate room during installations. 2) Our installers will be practice social distancing, to remain 6 feet from any customer. 3) Our installers will also be practicing social distancing from each other, except as needed for safety during the install process. 4) Installers will practice hand sanitizing, use masks and gloves while inside the home, and clean every surface touched before leaving the jobsite each day. 5) Whenever possible, we will minimize the number of employees who enter a building. 6) Trucks, tools, and materials are cleaned and sanitized daily. 7) Documents that require customer signatures will be reviewed in person, but sent & received electronically whenever possible. We ask that you return documents with a digital signature, send a photo of the signed documents or email with confirmation if a printed copy is not possible. 8) Please call payments into the office at 206-402-4229 rather than providing payment directly to the installer.
We will be closely monitoring the situation and will revised procedures as necessary. We hope these procedures will help us all finish the projects safely and effectively. Please reach out to our office directly at 206-402-4229 or operations@soundviewseattle.com with any questions, and thanks again! -Sound View Window & Door

Sound View recently installed a new Rogue Valley 42G Fir entry door with satin etch glass sidelights and transom window above the door in Edmonds, WA. The door features oil rubbed bronze hinges and 4 lites and shaker square sticking. The exterior was trimmed with 5/4 x 4 vg fir and the interior was wrapped with 1 x 4 pine and an oak floor transition.

For information on door and window installation contact Sound View Window & Door at 206-402-4229 or contact@soundviewseattle.com

item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com

[et_pb_section fb_built="1" admin_label="section" _builder_version="4.16" global_colors_info="{}" theme_builder_area="post_content"][et_pb_row admin_label="row" _builder_version="4.16" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat" global_colors_info="{}" theme_builder_area="post_content"][et_pb_column type="4_4" _builder_version="4.16" custom_padding="|||" global_colors_info="{}" custom_padding__hover="|||" theme_builder_area="post_content"][et_pb_text admin_label="Text" _builder_version="4.21.0" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat" global_colors_info="{}" theme_builder_area="post_content"]

Recent Milgard Trinsic window and patio door installation in Lake City in Seattle, WA. This project featured Milgard Trinsic horizontal sliding windows, casement windows, picture windows, awning windows, single hung windows and sliding glass patio doors. Glass type was suncoat low e glass with white vinyl framing. The product also included Matelux obscure glass in at least 1 window. The product was installed with a nail fin using a siding and liner cut back installation method using 2 x 2 primed cedar exterior trim. On some windows, we also installed a new stool and apron using 1 x 6 pine and 1 x 3 pine.

For information on installing new Milgard Trinsic windows and doors in your home, please contact Sound View Window & Door at 206-402-4229 or email at contact@soundviewseattle.com

Recent Milgard Trinsic window and patio door installation in Lake City in Seattle, WA. This project featured Milgard Trinsic horizontal sliding windows, casement windows, picture windows, awning windows, single hung windows and sliding glass patio doors. On some windows, we also installed a new stool and apron using 1 x 6 pine and 1 x 3 pine.

Sound View recently installed this solid wood fir plank door in Redmond, WA. The door was manufactured by Rogue Valley Doors and is model 7026. The door was finished with a clear coat. Installation was completed using 2 x 4 vg fir at the head and 2" vg fir brick mold on the legs on the exterior trim. The interior trim was completed with 1 x 4 vg fir at the head of the door and 1 x 3 vg fir on the legs. An oak floor transition as also applied.

For information on installing a new Rogue Valley wood door in your home, please contact Sound View Window & Door at 206-402-4229 or email at contact@soundviewseattle.com

item.title: Milgard V300 Trinsic Casement Window on Display in Bellevue Showroom
item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com
item.content:encoded: This display is available to view at our Bellevue showroom Interior color: Black Exterior color: Black Milgard V300 Trinsic Series Brochure The Milgard V300 Trinsic Series Sliding Patio Doors offer a perfect blend of modern aesthetics and functionality. Here are the key features: Modern Design: These vinyl patio doors have a sleek, contemporary look, making them ideal for both new construction and replacement projects. item.content:encoded: [gallery columns="2" size="medium" ids="21328,21329"] This display is available to view at our Bellevue showroom Interior color: White Exterior color: Black Milgard V300 Trinsic Series Brochure The Milgard V300 Trinsic Series Single-Hung Windows combine modern design with practical functionality. Here are the key details: Operation: These windows open and close easily in an up-and-down motion. The redesigned SmartTouch® window lock and handle is unique to this modern window series. When closed, the hardware practically disappears from view, maintaining the contemporary feel of the windows. Frame Options: Interior Frame Colors: Available in White, Tan, and Black. Exterior Frame Colors: Options include White, Tan, Silver, Classic Brown, Espresso, and Bronze Black. Glass Options: Standard Milgard SunCoat® Low-E2 Glass comes standard on all dual-pane windows. Tinted glass options: Cardinal Low-E Solar Bronze and Solar Gray. Obscure glass options: #42 Clear, Aquatex, Delta Frost, Frosted Glue Chip, Satin Etch, Narrow Reed, P516 Rain. Grid Styles: Express your creativity and enhance curb appeal with various grid options: Flat Grid Sculptured Grid Simulated Divided Lite (SDL) with a 2-1/4" Check Rail Hardware: The SmartTouch® window lock has a squared-off profile that blends into the frame and practically disappears from view. Modern Design: Constructed from durable vinyl that won’t absorb moisture and doesn’t require painting. Even sightlines across the series allow mixing and matching while maintaining a cohesive look from top to bottom. Whether you’re replacing existing windows or planning new construction, the Milgard V300 Trinsic Single-Hung Windows offer both style and functionality.

item.title: Andersen 100 Series Casement Window Display in Bellevue Showroom
item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com
item.content:encoded: [gallery columns="2" size="medium" ids="21448,21447"] Interior color: White Exterior color: White 100-series-product-guide The Andersen 100 Series Casement Windows offer a blend of modern design, energy efficiency, and low maintenance. Here are the key features: Material: Made with revolutionary Fibrex® composite material, which is twice as strong as vinyl. Fibrex® combines the best qualities of wood and vinyl, providing durability, thermal insulation, and resistance to rot, fading, flaking, blistering, and peeling. Colors: Available in five exterior and four internal deep, rich colors that won’t fade or require extensive maintenance. The color options allow you to personalize the windows to match your home’s character. Sizes: These casement windows can be up to 3 feet wide and 6 feet high. Custom sizes are available in 1/8-inch increments, making it possible to fit almost any space with fresh air and natural light. Hardware and Grilles: Choose from two hardware styles with up to six finish options. Standard and custom grille patterns let you personalize the final look of your windows. Energy Efficiency: The Fibrex® material provides excellent thermal insulation, helping to keep your home comfortable year-round. Dual-pane glass with Low-E2 coating enhances energy efficiency. Security: Multi-point lock on the perimeter of the frame offers enhanced security. Whether you’re replacing existing windows or planning new construction, the Andersen 100 Series Casement Windows are a smart alternative to vinyl, combining style, durability, and energy efficiency.

Colors: Available in 5 exterior colors and 4 internal colors. These deep, rich colors won’t rot, fade, flake, blister, or peel, and they require minimal maintenance. Sizes: The 100 Series Single-Hung Window can be up to 4 feet wide and 7.6 feet high. Custom sizes are also available in 1/8-inch increments, allowing you to fit almost any space with fresh air and natural light. Accessories: Choose from 3 hardware styles with up to 6 finish options. Customize the grille patterns to match your home’s character. Warranty: Andersen offers a top warranty in the industry, providing peace of mind and added value. The warranties are even transferable if you sell your home. Explore the 100 Series Single-Hung Window in real homes by checking out the hashtag #andersenwindows on social media. If you’re looking for an affordable and reliable window option, the Andersen 100 Series is worth considering! 🏡🪟

item.content:encoded: [gallery columns="2" size="medium" ids="21563,21564"] 100-series-product-guide The Andersen 100 Series Gliding Window is a fantastic choice for homeowners seeking a blend of durability, energy efficiency, and aesthetic appeal. Material: Crafted with Fibrex® composite material, which is twice as strong as vinyl. Fibrex® ensures longevity, energy efficiency, and minimal maintenance. Configuration Options: Available in multiple configurations: Single Stationary Sash with One Gliding Sash: Ideal for simplicity and ventilation. Three-Sash Configuration: Features two gliding sashes that slide past a fixed center sash. These options allow you to customize based on your needs. Colors: Choose from 5 exterior colors and 4 internal colors. These deep, rich colors won’t rot, fade, flake, blister, or peel, ensuring long-lasting beauty. Sizes: The 100 Series Gliding Window can be up to 6 feet wide and 6 feet high. Custom sizes are available in 1/8-inch increments, allowing you to fill almost any space with fresh air and natural light. Hardware and Grille Options: Select from 3 hardware styles with up to 6 finish options. Personalize the final look with standard or custom grille patterns to match your home’s character. Benefits and Features: Low-Maintenance: Requires minimal upkeep, saving you time and effort. Energy-Efficient: The Fibrex® material provides excellent insulation, helping regulate indoor temperatures. Exceptional Value: You get quality and performance without breaking the bank. Transferable Warranty: Andersen offers top warranties, even if you sell your home. Explore the 100 Series Gliding Window in real homes by checking out the hashtag #andersenwindows on social media. For technical details, view the 100 Series limited warranty and explore sizing and performance documents. Andersen also offers other gliding window options like the 200 Series, 400 Series, and E-Series, each with unique features! 🏡🪟

item.title: Andersen E Series Casement Window Display in our Bellevue Showroom
item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com
item.content:encoded: [gallery columns="2" size="medium" ids="21543,21545"] E Series Brochure Design and Material: The E-Series casement window boasts a virtually maintenance-free aluminum exterior that resists water and stands up to the elements. It offers unmatched design freedom, allowing you to fully customize it to your preferences. You can order it in nearly any shape, size, color, interior wood species, or finish. Exterior and Interior Options: Colors: You have a wide range of choices with 50 exterior colors and 14 interior colors. Additionally, you can opt for natural, unfinished, or stained wood to achieve either a modern or traditional look. Custom colors are also available. Sizes: The E-Series casement window can be as wide as 3 feet and as high as 6 feet. Custom sizes are available in 1/8-inch increments, allowing you to fill almost any space with fresh air and natural light. Accessories and Personalization: Hardware Styles: You can select from various hardware styles, each with up to 10 finish options. Grille Patterns: Choose standard or custom grille patterns to match the character of your home. Energy Efficiency: The E-Series casement window offers triple-pane glass options, providing exceptional energy efficiency. Its weather-resistant design ensures it performs exceptionally well. Warranty: Every E-Series window and door comes with one of the industry’s best limited warranties. Plus, it’s transferable, adding value if you decide to sell your home. In summary, the Andersen E-Series Casement Window combines durability, customization, and energy efficiency, making it an excellent choice for homeowners seeking both functionality and aesthetics. 🏡🌟

item.content:encoded: [gallery columns="2" size="medium" ids="21539,21540"] E Series Brochure Design and Material: The E-Series double-hung window features two operating sashes that move up and down, allowing for ventilation from the top, bottom, or both. The sashes tilt inwards, making cleaning from the inside a breeze. Constructed with wood protected by an aluminum exterior, this window offers durability and customization. Exterior and Interior Options: Colors: You have a plethora of choices! Select from 50 exterior colors and 14 interior colors. Additionally, opt for natural, unfinished, or stained wood to achieve a modern or traditional look. Custom colors are also available. Sizes: The E-Series double-hung window can be as wide as 4 feet and as high as 7 feet 6 inches. Custom sizes are available in 1/8-inch increments, allowing you to fill almost any space with fresh air and natural light. Accessories and Personalization: Hardware Styles: Choose from two hardware styles with up to 10 finish options. Grille Patterns: Personalize the final look with standard or custom grille patterns that match your home’s character. Energy Efficiency: The E-Series double-hung window offers triple-pane glass options, ensuring exceptional energy efficiency. Its weather-resistant design ensures optimal performance. Warranty: Every E-Series window and door comes with one of the industry’s best limited warranties. Plus, it’s transferable, adding value if you decide to sell your home. In summary, the Andersen E-Series Double-Hung Window combines functionality, aesthetics, and energy efficiency, making it an excellent choice for homeowners seeking quality and style. 🏡✨

item.title: FAQ - Why do new windows have condensation?
item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com
item.content:encoded: Condensation is a normal occurrence on windows, and it can happen on new windows for a number of reasons: Warm, moist air meets a cooler surface. Condensation happens when warm, moist air comes into contact with a cooler surface, like window glass. This can happen on the inside of windows when the glass is colder than the air inside the home, or on the outside of windows when the air is warmer than the glass. Windows are well-insulated Condensation on the outside of new windows can be a sign that the windows are well-insulated. This is because the window's surface temperature drops below the dew point, which is the temperature at which the air is 100% saturated with moisture. Low-E glass Low-E glass is a thin coating of metal that reflects heat and energy, keeping the glass temperature closer to the outside temperature. Tight seals Condensation can be a sign that your windows have good, tight seals. However, a tightly sealed home can also retain more humidity, which can lead to condensation. Everyday activities Activities like cooking, bathing, and breathing all contribute to the humidity in your home

item.title: Clear Glass vs. Low-E Glass: What's the Difference and Which is Right for Your Home?
item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com
item.content:encoded: When it comes to choosing windows for your home, you're faced with a dizzying array of options. One of the most important choices you'll make is the type of glass. Two of the most common options are clear glass and low-E glass. But what's the difference, and which is right for you? Clear Glass: A Simple Solution Clear glass is just what it sounds like: glass with no special coatings or treatments. It's the traditional choice for windows and offers a clear, unobstructed view. Pros: High light transmission: Clear glass allows maximum natural light into your home. Affordable: It's typically the most budget-friendly option. Cons: Poor energy efficiency: Clear glass doesn't do much to regulate temperature. It allows heat to easily escape in the winter and enter in the summer, leading to higher energy bills. Increased UV damage: Clear glass allows more UV rays to pass through, which can fade furniture and carpets over time. Low-E Glass: Energy Efficiency and More Low-E glass (short for low-emissivity) has a special coating that reflects heat. This coating helps to keep your home warmer in the winter and cooler in the summer, resulting in significant energy savings. Pros: Energy-efficient: Low-E glass can significantly reduce your heating and cooling costs. UV protection: The coating helps to block harmful UV rays, protecting your furniture and flooring from fading. Improved comfort: Low-E glass helps to maintain a more consistent temperature throughout your home. Cons: Higher cost: Low-E glass is typically more expensive than clear glass. Slightly reduced visible light transmission: The coating can slightly reduce the amount of natural light that enters your home (though this is often minimal). Which is Right for You? The best choice for your home depends on your priorities and climate. Consider low-E glass if: You live in an area with extreme temperatures. You want to reduce your energy bills. You're concerned about UV damage to your furnishings. Clear glass might be suitable if: You live in a mild climate. You're on a tight budget. Maximizing natural light is your top priority. Beyond the Basics There are different types of low-E coatings, each designed for specific climates. For example, some coatings are better at reflecting heat away from your home (ideal for hot climates), while others are better at keeping heat inside (ideal for cold climates). Talk to the Experts If you're unsure which type of glass is right for you, consult with one of our product consultants. They can help you assess your needs and recommend the best option for your home and budget. By understanding the differences between clear glass and low-E glass, you can make an informed decision that will enhance your home's comfort, energy efficiency, and value for years to come. item.title: Washington State Egress Window Requirements: A Homeowner's Guide
item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com
item.content:encoded: Egress windows are a critical safety feature in any home, providing a means of escape in case of fire or other emergencies. In Washington State, specific requirements must be met for egress windows to be considered legally compliant. Let's break down the essential elements: 1. Size Matters: * Minimum Opening Area: The window must have a minimum net clear opening area of 5.7 square feet. This means the actual space you can crawl through must meet this measurement. * Height and Width: The opening must be at least 24 inches high and 20 inches wide. * Exception: For basement windows (below grade), the minimum net clear opening area is 5 square feet. 2. Accessibility is Key: * Sill Height: The window sill cannot be more than 44 inches above the floor. * Easy Operation: The window must open easily from the inside without the need for keys, tools, or special knowledge. 3. Window Wells (for basement windows): * Minimum Size: If the window sill is below ground level, a window well is required. It must be at least 9 square feet in area, with specific dimensions for width, height, and projection depending on the well depth. * Escape Ladder: If the window well is deeper than 44 inches, a permanently affixed ladder or steps are required for safe egress. 4. Other Considerations: * Obstructions: The window opening must be free of any bars or grilles that would hinder escape. If security bars are used, they must have a quick-release mechanism that can be easily operated from the inside. * Emergency Escape Under Decks: If an egress window is located under a deck or porch, it needs a clear, unobstructed pathway to a yard or court. This pathway must be at least 36 inches high and wide. Why are Egress Windows Important? Egress windows are not just about escaping a fire; they also: * Provide natural light and ventilation * Increase the value of your home * Can serve as a secondary means of entry for emergency personnel Do I Need to Upgrade My Windows? If you're unsure whether your windows meet Washington State's egress requirements, it's best to consult with a qualified contractor or building inspector. They can assess your windows and advise you on any necessary upgrades. Remember: Safety is paramount. Investing in compliant egress windows provides peace of mind and ensures the well-being of your family in an emergency. Disclaimer: This blog post provides a general overview of egress window requirements in Washington State. Always refer to the most current building codes and consult with professionals for specific guidance on your project.

item.title: Framing the View: Andersen E-Series Standard vs. Auxiliary Picture Windows
item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com
item.content:encoded: Choosing the right windows for your home is a crucial decision, impacting everything from aesthetics and energy efficiency to natural light and views. Within Andersen's esteemed E-Series, the picture window offers a beautiful, stationary way to bring the outdoors in. But even within this category, there are choices to be made, specifically regarding the frame. This article explores the key differences between the standard and auxiliary frame options for Andersen E-Series picture windows, helping you determine which best suits your needs and style. Standard Picture Window Frame: A Classic Presence The standard frame on an Andersen E-Series picture window is characterized by its substantial profile. This wider frame creates a more traditional, robust look, often complementing homes with classic or historical architectural styles. Think of it as the window's "picture frame," adding a noticeable border to the view. Visual Impact: The standard frame makes a bolder statement. It draws the eye and can become a design element in itself. Energy Performance: Due to its larger size, the standard frame can contribute to enhanced insulation, potentially improving energy efficiency. Traditional Appeal: This frame style aligns well with traditional, colonial, or craftsman-style homes. Auxiliary Picture Window Frame: A Modern Touch The auxiliary frame, also known as a narrow frame, offers a more contemporary and minimalist aesthetic. Its slimmer profile prioritizes the view, minimizing the frame's visual presence and maximizing the glass area. This results in a cleaner, more streamlined look that's particularly popular in modern and contemporary homes. Unobstructed Views: The narrow frame allows for a less obstructed view of the outdoors, creating a stronger connection with the landscape. Modern Aesthetic: Its clean lines and minimal design complement modern, contemporary, and even industrial-style homes. Maximum Light: The reduced frame size maximizes the glass area, allowing more natural light to flood the interior space. Key Differences Summarized: Feature Standard Frame Auxiliary Frame Frame Width Wider, more substantial Narrower, more minimal Visual Impact Bolder, more prominent Subtler, less noticeable Aesthetic Traditional, classic Modern, contemporary View Framed, defined Less obstructed, expansive Light Good Maximum Energy Efficiency Potentially higher due to size Generally good Choosing the Right Frame: The best choice depends on several factors: Architectural Style: Match the frame style to the overall architecture of your home. Personal Preference: Consider your aesthetic preferences and the desired look for your space. Do you want the frame to be a design element, or do you prefer it to blend seamlessly with the surroundings? View: If you have a particularly stunning view, the auxiliary frame's minimal profile will help showcase it. Light: If maximizing natural light is a priority, the auxiliary frame's larger glass area is the better choice. Ultimately, both the standard and auxiliary frames offer excellent quality and performance. Visiting an Andersen showroom or consulting with a window professional is highly recommended. Seeing the frames in person and discussing your project goals will help you make an informed decision and choose the perfect picture window for your home.

item.title: Milgard Spring Promo 2025
item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com
item.content:encoded: SPRING PROMO FLYER Rebate Summary: Milgard is offering a rebate on the purchase of qualifying windows and patio doors.   Savings are provided in the form of electronic gift cards.   Key Dates and Rules for Rebate Redemption: Purchase Period: Products must be purchased between April 14, 2025, and June 9, 2025.   Eligible Products: V250 Style Line Series, V300 Trinsic™ Series, or V400 Tuscany Series windows and V300 Trinsic™ Series or V400 Tuscany Series patio doors.   Rebate Amounts: $100 per qualifying patio door   $40 per V400 Tuscany Series window   $30 per V300 Trinsic™ Series window   $20 per V250 Style Line Series window   $20 bonus per product with capstock   Registration Deadline: To qualify, homeowners must register online at milgard.com/promo-registration by August 4, 2025, using the promo code SPRING2025 and their Sales Order Number. Registrations after 11:59 PM on this date will not be eligible.   Gift Card Delivery: Electronic gift cards will be sent approximately 12 weeks after delivery or registration, whichever is later.   Eligibility: Offer is for homeowners only. Dealers, contractors, and builders are not eligible. The offer cannot be transferred, combined with other offers, redeemed for cash, or combined with special pricing or previously discounted orders.   Purchases: Must be made through participating Milgard Certified Dealers in specific regions (WA, OR, CA, AZ, NM, CO, ID, MT, NV, UT, AK, HI, and Canada) and are not valid through Home Depot or Lowe's.   Right to Modify: Milgard reserves the right to amend or terminate the promotion at any time without notice.

item.title: Awning window vs horizontal sliding window in a high exposure area
item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com
item.content:encoded:
For a highly exposed wall with no overhang protection, an awning window is significantly better for water management than a horizontal sliding window. Here's a breakdown of why:
  • Design for Rain Protection: An awning window is hinged at the top and opens outward from the bottom. This design creates a canopy or "awning" over the opening. This feature allows you to open the window for ventilation even during light or moderate rain, as the angled glass and frame prevent water from coming inside. The water simply runs off the exterior surface.
  • Superior Sealing: Awning windows use a compression seal, which creates a tight, airtight seal when the window is closed and locked. This compression seal is highly effective at preventing air and moisture from leaking in, which is crucial for a wall that will be directly hit by wind-driven rain.
  • Poor Water Management of Sliding Windows: Horizontal sliding windows operate by having one or more sashes slide along a track. The seals on these types of windows are not a compression seal; they are often flexible brushes or strips that allow the window to move. This can create a gap where air and, more importantly, water can seep through. The tracks on sliding windows can also collect dirt and debris, which can clog the weep holes (drainage holes) and cause water to overflow into the interior of your home, especially during heavy, wind-driven rain.
In a situation where a wall is highly exposed with no overhang, a window's ability to resist direct water penetration is paramount. The design of the awning window is specifically engineered for this purpose, while a sliding window's design is more susceptible to water infiltration.

item.title: Project Showcase: A Full Home Window & Door Transformation in Edmonds, WA
item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com
item.content:encoded:
We recently wrapped up an exciting and comprehensive window and door replacement project for a homeowner in the Edmonds, WA area! This extensive remodel involved replacing nearly two dozen existing units across two floors, significantly boosting the home's energy efficiency, curb appeal, and functionality.

The Scope of Work

The project involved a full tear-out and replacement of 23 units.. The replacement units were chosen from Milgard's popular vinyl product lines, ensuring durability and high performance:

Milgard V300 Trinsic Vinyl: Used for all sliding windows and sliding patio doors.. These provide a clean, contemporary look with excellent operability3

Milgard V250 Style Line Vinyl: Selected for the picture windows.. This series offers slim frames that maximize the viewable glass area.

Key Product Highlights

The new windows and doors feature key upgrades designed to improve the home's comfort and energy savings:

Color Consistency: All units, both interior and exterior, were specified in White for a cohesive and bright look against the home’s exterior siding.

Energy-Efficient Glass: Most units were outfitted with SuncoatMax Clear with LowE or Suncoat Clear with LowE glass.. Low-E coatings are essential for managing solar heat gain and improving insulation, which is crucial for Seattle-area weather8.

Specialty Glass: For one of the Front Bedroom windows, we installed a Suncoat Obscure with LowE glass with a frosted stain etched finish.. This provides privacy without sacrificing natural light.

Sliding Doors: We installed three new sliding patio doors in the Den, Dining Room, and another area, all featuring White hardware and upgraded keyed screen surrounds for security and convenience.

Installation Details

Our installation process was meticulous to ensure a clean finish and proper weatherproofing:

Full Frame Installation: We utilized a nailing flange installation method for a secure and watertight seal

Exterior Trim: To ensure a clean, professional transition, we applied 5/4 x 2 primed cedar exterior trim around all the new units. This material is primed and ready for the homeowner to paint to match their exterior color perfectly.

Window Remodeling: We even managed a major change in the Master Bedroom by dropping the sill a full 12 inches to accommodate a new $96^{\prime\prime} \times 48^{\prime\prime}$ horizontal sliding window

item.title: What are the benefits of choosing Milgard windows?
item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com
item.content:encoded:
Choosing Milgard windows is an excellent decision for homeowners in the Pacific Northwest, as they are engineered specifically for the regional climate.

In Seattle, you can visit Sound View Window and Door to see these windows in person. Each of the series listed below is on display at their showroom, allowing you to test the hardware and compare the frame finishes before making a decision.

1. Industry-Leading Full Lifetime Warranty

Milgard offers a Full Lifetime Warranty that is a cut above the industry standard.

  • Parts and Labor: Unlike many warranties that only cover the window itself, Milgard covers both the components and the labor to fix them for as long as you own your home.

  • Transferability: If you sell your home, the warranty is transferable to the next owner for up to 10 years, which is a significant selling point for buyers.

2. High-Quality, In-House Materials

Milgard controls the quality of their products by manufacturing their own materials.

  • Vinyl Formula: They use a signature vinyl compound designed to resist the specific UV and moisture challenges of the West Coast, preventing the "yellowing" or cracking often seen in cheaper vinyl.

  • Fiberglass Strength: Their Ultra series uses pultruded fiberglass, which is incredibly strong and expands at nearly the same rate as the glass itself, protecting the seals from failing during temperature swings.

3. Custom Sizing at No Extra Cost

Milgard windows are custom-made to your exact measurements. While other brands often charge a "custom size" premium, Milgard treats custom dimensions as their standard, making them ideal for remodeling projects where standard "off-the-shelf" sizes rarely fit.

Milgard Series on Display at Sound View Window and Door

You can view and test each of these series at their showrooms:

  • Tuscany® (V400): Premium vinyl with a traditional look.

  • Trinsic™ (V300): Contemporary vinyl with a narrow frame.

  • Ultra™ (C650): Maximum durability fiberglass.

  • Style Line® (V250): A sleek, clean-lined, and affordable vinyl option.

  • Thermally Improved Aluminum (A250): Features a thermal break for energy efficiency while maintaining a slim, industrial profile.

Showroom Locations

  • Seattle (Queen Anne): 921 Elliott Ave W, Seattle, WA 98119

  • Seattle (Lake City): 12301 Lake City Way NE, Seattle, WA 98125

  • Bellevue: Open by appointment only. Please contact Sound View to schedule a time to visit this location.

item.title: Maximize Your Home’s Safety with the Milgard SecurityMax™ Package
item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com
item.content:encoded:
[embed]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4oY5pthxB3E[/embed]  

When it comes to your home, peace of mind is priceless. We all want to feel secure, but nobody wants to deal with clunky, difficult-to-operate locks that compromise the aesthetic of their patio doors.

In our latest featured video [link to video], we take a closer look at the Milgard SecurityMax™ Package, a revolutionary security system designed exclusively for the Tuscany® Series sliding patio doors.

What Makes SecurityMax Different?

Most sliding doors rely on a single latch, which can be a weak point in home security. The SecurityMax package upgrades your protection by combining two innovative technologies into one powerhouse system:

  1. Multi-Point Locking System: With a single motion, the door engages four different locking points. This secures the door firmly into the top frame, the bottom track, and at the handle, making forced entry nearly impossible.

  2. The SmartTouch® Bolt: This is a fully integrated steel bolt that acts as a secondary lock. With a simple flip of a lever, it secures the door into the top frame.

Security Meets Convenience

One of the best features of the SecurityMax system is its versatility. Not only does it exceed California’s rigorous forced-entry codes by over 25%, but it also allows for a "vented" locked position. This means you can enjoy fresh air while knowing your door is still securely bolted and safe from intruders.

Upgrade Your Home Today

Your family’s safety shouldn’t be a DIY project. At Sound View Window & Door, we specialize in the professional installation of Milgard products. We ensure that your new patio doors are fitted with precision so that every locking point works exactly as intended.

Ready to upgrade your home security? Contact Sound View Window & Door today for more information or to schedule your free estimate.

  • Phone: 206-402-4229

  • Website: www.soundviewwindowanddoor.com

  • Visit Us: Stop by our Seattle showroom to see the SecurityMax system in action!

item.title: The Seattle Homeowner’s Guide to Windows: Is Triple-Pane Worth the Upgrade?
item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com
item.content:encoded:
If you’ve started shopping for windows in the Puget Sound area, you’ve likely encountered a technical crossroads: Double-Pane vs. Triple-Pane. In a city like Seattle—where we balance damp winters, increasing summer smoke seasons, and the constant hum of the I-5 or Sea-Tac flight paths—this isn't just a matter of price. It’s a matter of long-term comfort. To help navigate this, we’ve teamed up with the experts at Sound View Window & Door to break down the science, the regional benefits, and the trade-offs you won’t find on a standard sales brochure.

The Core Difference: Layers of Protection

At its simplest, the distinction is about the "Insulated Glass Unit" (IGU).

  • Double-Pane Windows: Two panes of glass with a spacer and an insulating gas (usually Argon) sealed between them.

  • Triple-Pane Windows: A third pane of glass creates two separate chambers of insulating gas, significantly boosting the window's resistance to heat flow.

Why Seattle Homeowners Ask About Triple-Pane

Sound View Window & Door notes that Seattleites usually have two primary motivations for eyeing the triple-pane upgrade:

  1. Thermal Comfort: In the Northwest, we don't just deal with cold; we deal with "the chill." Triple-pane windows keep the interior glass temperature closer to the room temperature, eliminating that "drafty" feeling when you sit near a window in January.

  2. Sound Attenuation: With density increasing in neighborhoods from Ballard to Columbia City, street noise is a top-tier concern. Triple-pane is often marketed as the ultimate "noise killer."

The Hidden Trade-offs: What You Sacrifice for the Third Pane

While more glass sounds like a win, it comes with physical and functional compromises that every homeowner should weigh before signing a contract.

1. The Weight Factor

Triple-pane units are roughly 50% heavier than double-pane. For an older Seattle craftsman or a home with settling issues, this added weight can put a strain on the original rough openings. You may find that your hardware (cranks and hinges) wears out faster over decades of use because it is fighting gravity to move a much heavier sash.

2. Natural Light Transmission

Every layer of glass reflects a small percentage of visible light. In the "Big Dark" of a Seattle winter, every lumen counts. According to Energy Star, triple-pane windows can have a lower Visible Transmittance (VT) rating, meaning your home might feel subtly dimmer than with double-pane glass.

3. The "Resonance" Trap in Sound Control

Surprisingly, a standard triple-pane window isn't always the best at stopping noise. If all three panes are the same thickness, they can vibrate at the same frequency, occasionally failing to block low-frequency rumbles like heavy trucks.

Smart Alternatives: Getting Performance Without the Bulk

If the weight or cost of triple-pane feels like overkill, Sound View Window & Door often points clients toward "engineered" double-pane solutions that solve specific problems more efficiently.

For Better Sound: Dissimilar or Laminated Glass

Instead of adding a third pane, you can use Dissimilar Glass—pairing a 3mm pane with a 5mm pane in a double-pane unit. Because the panes have different masses, they vibrate at different frequencies, "breaking" the sound wave. As noted by the National Fenestration Rating Council (NFRC), varying glass thickness is one of the most effective ways to improve a window's Sound Transmission Class (STC) rating. For extreme noise, Laminated Glass (a plastic interlayer between glass) acts as a shock absorber, often outperforming triple-pane.

For Better Heat: Fourth-Surface Coatings

To mimic triple-pane warmth without the heavy third layer, you can opt for a Fourth-Surface Low-E coating. This is a specialized film applied to the side of the glass facing your living room. It reflects radiant heat back into your home, providing an "insulation boost" that brings a double-pane window very close to triple-pane performance levels.

The Verdict: Which is right for you?

Priority Recommended Choice
Budget & Light High-Performance Double-Pane
Maximum Energy Efficiency Triple-Pane
Traffic/City Noise Double-Pane with Laminated or Dissimilar Glass
Extreme Draft Sensitivity Triple-Pane

Ultimately, there is no one-size-fits-all. A home in a quiet cul-de-sac in Shoreline has different needs than a condo overlooking the West Seattle Bridge. Ready to see the difference in person? Explore our window manufacturers to see which brands offer these high-performance options.

item.content:encoded:

Indow Acoustic Window Inserts: Reduce Noise and Improve Comfort — Installed by Sound View Window and Door

Indow Acoustic Window Inserts: Reduce Noise and Improve Comfort — Installed by Sound View Window and Door

Indow Acoustic Window Inserts are an innovative solution designed to significantly reduce noise and enhance indoor comfort. These inserts utilize advanced soundproofing technology to create a quieter living environment, making them an ideal choice for urban dwellers or anyone seeking peace in their home. This article will explore how Indow inserts work, the installation process by Sound View Window and Door, and the benefits of choosing these inserts over traditional window replacement. By understanding the advantages of “retrofit window soundproofing”, homeowners can make informed decisions that improve their living spaces.

How Do Indow Acoustic Window Inserts Reduce Noise and Enhance Comfort?

Indow Acoustic Window Inserts effectively reduce noise by utilizing a combination of acoustic materials and precise engineering. These inserts fit snugly within existing window frames, creating an additional barrier that dampens sound waves. The result is a noticeable decrease in external noise, leading to a more serene indoor atmosphere. Users often report significant improvements in comfort, as the inserts also help regulate indoor temperatures, making homes more energy-efficient.

What Is the Noise Reduction Technology Behind Indow Inserts?

The technology behind Indow Acoustic Window Inserts involves the use of specialized acoustic materials that absorb and block sound. These materials are designed to minimize sound transmission, effectively reducing noise pollution from outside. The inserts are engineered to fit tightly within the window frame, ensuring that there are no gaps for sound to penetrate. This innovative approach allows for a quieter home environment without the need for costly window replacements.

How Do Window Insulation Inserts Improve Indoor Comfort?

In addition to noise reduction, Indow inserts enhance indoor comfort by improving thermal insulation. They help maintain consistent indoor temperatures by reducing drafts and heat loss during colder months. This not only contributes to a more comfortable living space but also leads to energy savings. Homeowners can enjoy a cozy environment while potentially lowering their heating and cooling costs.

What Is the Installation Process by Sound View Window and Door in Seattle?

The installation process for Indow Acoustic Window Inserts by Sound View Window and Door is straightforward and non-invasive. The team measures the existing window frames to create custom inserts that fit perfectly. This method allows homeowners to retain their original windows while benefiting from enhanced soundproofing and insulation.

How Are Indow Acoustic Window Inserts Installed Without Replacing Windows?

Indow inserts are installed without the need to replace existing windows, making the process efficient and cost-effective. The installation involves placing the inserts into the window frames, where they are held in place by a compression fit. This non-invasive method ensures that the integrity of the original windows is maintained while providing the benefits of modern soundproofing technology.

What Is the Typical Installation Timeline and Local Expertise Offered?

The typical installation timeline for Indow Acoustic Window Inserts is relatively quick, often completed within a few hours depending on the number of windows being treated. Sound View Window and Door brings local expertise to the process, ensuring that each installation is performed with precision and care. Their team is knowledgeable about the specific needs of Seattle homes, providing tailored solutions for optimal performance.

Why Choose Indow Acoustic Window Inserts Over Full Window Replacement?

Choosing Indow Acoustic Window Inserts over full window replacement offers several advantages. First, the cost-effectiveness of inserts makes them an attractive option for homeowners looking to improve their living spaces without the financial burden of new windows. Additionally, the installation process is much simpler and quicker, allowing homeowners to enjoy the benefits of soundproofing without extensive renovations.

What Are the Benefits of Retrofit Window Soundproofing Compared to Replacement?

Retrofit window soundproofing, such as Indow inserts, provides effective noise reduction while preserving the original windows. This approach is less disruptive and can be completed in a fraction of the time compared to full window replacement. Homeowners can enjoy the benefits of improved comfort and energy efficiency without the hassle of major construction work.

How Do Energy Efficient Window Inserts Save Costs and Improve Comfort?

Energy-efficient window inserts not only enhance comfort by maintaining consistent indoor temperatures but also lead to significant cost savings on energy bills. By reducing heat loss and drafts, homeowners can lower their heating and cooling expenses. This dual benefit of comfort and cost-effectiveness makes Indow inserts a smart investment for any homeowner.

How Can Customers Get Pricing, Free Estimates, and Visit the Showroom?

Customers interested in Indow Acoustic Window Inserts can easily obtain pricing and free estimates by contacting Sound View Window and Door. The company offers consultations to discuss specific needs and provide tailored solutions. Additionally, customers are welcome to visit their showrooms to see the products in person and learn more about the installation process.

What Are the Pricing Options and Financing for Indow Acoustic Window Inserts?

Sound View Window and Door provides various pricing options for Indow Acoustic Window Inserts, ensuring that customers can find a solution that fits their budget. Financing options are also available, making it easier for homeowners to invest in soundproofing solutions without financial strain.

How to Schedule a Free Estimate or Showroom Visit with Sound View Window and Door?

Scheduling a free estimate or showroom visit with Sound View Window and Door is simple. Customers can reach out via phone at (206) 572-3411 to set up an appointment. The team is ready to assist with any questions and guide customers through the process of enhancing their home comfort with Indow Acoustic Window Inserts.

item.title: Milgard Spring 2026 Promotion
item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com
item.content:encoded:
Boost Your Home’s Value This Spring with the Milgard Tax Refund Reward!

Tax season is here, and while a refund is always a welcome sight, Sound View Window & Door wants to help you make yours work even harder. If you’ve been waiting for the right moment to upgrade your home’s comfort, style, and energy efficiency, that moment has officially arrived.

 

From April 13 through June 8, 2026, Milgard is offering a major reward promotion that can put money back in your pocket for every window and patio door you replace.

 

Invest in Your Home, Get Rewarded

Why just spend your tax refund when you can invest it? By upgrading to high-quality Milgard products, you aren't just improving your daily view—you’re boosting your home’s long-term value.

Depending on the series you choose, you can earn an electronic gift card for every single unit you purchase:

 
Qualifying Product Reward Amount
V400 Tuscany® or V300 Trinsic™ Patio Doors

$100 Reward per door

 
V400 Tuscany® Series Windows

$40 Reward per window

 
V300 Trinsic™ Series Windows

$30 Reward per window

 
V250 Style Line® Series Windows

$20 Reward per window

 

How to Claim Your Reward

Getting your gift card is a simple, three-step process:

  1. Purchase: Place your order for qualifying Milgard windows or patio doors through Sound View Window & Door between April 13 and June 8, 2026.

  2. Register: Visit milgard.com/promo-registration by August 3, 2026. Use the promo code SPRING2026 and have your Sales Order Number ready (we’ll provide this to you!).

  3. Enjoy: Once your product is delivered and your registration is processed, you’ll receive your electronic gift card via email in approximately 12 weeks.

Ready to Start Your Spring Transformation?

Don't wait—this offer is only available for a limited time and is exclusively for homeowners. Skip the big-box retailers and work with the local experts who can ensure your project is done right.

Contact Sound View Window & Door today to schedule your consultation and make the most of your 2026 tax refund!

Note: Offer valid for homeowners only. Not valid for purchases through Home Depot or Lowe's. Registrations must be submitted by 11:59pm PST on August 3, 2026.

item.title: Walk-In Shower Ideas for Small Pacific Northwest Bathrooms
item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com
item.content:encoded:
Walk-In Shower Ideas for Small Pacific Northwest Bathrooms

Living in the Pacific Northwest means embracing a certain lifestyle: stunning landscapes, cozy rainy days, and a deep appreciation for natural beauty. But it also often means dealing with older craftsman homes or compact mid-century builds with notoriously small bathrooms.

When square footage is tight, a traditional tub-and-shower combo can make your bathroom feel dark and cramped. Enter the walk-in shower. By removing visual barriers and optimizing layout, you can turn even the tiniest PNW bathroom into a bright, spa-like sanctuary.

Here are five design ideas tailored specifically for bringing open, airy, and functional walk-in showers into compact Pacific Northwest homes.

1. The Seamless Wet Room Concept

In a truly small bathroom, separating the shower from the rest of the space with walls or heavy glass doors can make the room feel like a series of closets. Instead, look to the European-style wet room.

By waterproofing the entire bathroom floor and installing a curbless walk-in shower, the boundaries disappear.

  • Why it works for the PNW: It maximizes every square inch of a small footprint and makes cleanup incredibly easy after a muddy hike or a rainy dog walk.

  • Design Tip: Use a single, continuous tile from the bathroom floor right into the shower to trick the eye into thinking the space is much larger than it is.

2. Embrace "Biophilic" PNW Textures

Just because a shower is small doesn't mean it has to feel clinical. The Pacific Northwest is famous for biophilic design—bringing the textures of the outdoors inside.

Material Visual Effect Vibe
Pebble Tile Floors Adds organic texture underfoot Mountain stream
Earthy Green Subway Tile Reflects light while adding depth Cascade forest
Matte Black Fixtures Provides sharp, modern contrast Moody Puget Sound
Cedar Accents (Outside splash zone) Warms up cool tile tones Cozy A-frame cabin

Using vertical stacked tiles in deep forest greens, misty grays, or ocean blues can draw the eye upward, making low ceilings feel significantly higher.

3. The "Floating" Glass Shield

If a full wet room isn't your style, skip the traditional swinging glass door. In a small bathroom, a door needs clearance to swing open, which wastes valuable floor space.

Instead, opt for a single, fixed floating glass panel (often called a walk-in shower screen).

  • It keeps the water contained to the spray zone.

  • It eliminates bulky chrome frames that clutter the sightline.

  • It allows natural light from your bathroom window to flood the entire space, keeping those gloomy winter mornings a bit brighter.

4. Utilize Smart Recessed Storage

When space is at a premium, the last thing you want is a plastic caddy hanging from your showerhead, overflowing with shampoo bottles. It clutters the space visually and physically.

Instead, build recessed shower niches between the wall studs.

Pro Tip: Go horizontal instead of vertical. A long, horizontal recessed shelf running along the main wall of your walk-in shower provides ample storage for all your locally made, clean-beauty products without taking up an inch of elbow room.

5. Skylights and High Windows

We all know that natural light can be a hot commodity during a PNW winter. If your small bathroom shares an exterior wall or sits directly under the roof, consider adding a transom window (a high, narrow window) or a sun tunnel directly above the walk-in shower.

This provides absolute privacy while channeling whatever daylight is available straight into your morning routine. Plus, there is nothing quite like showering while watching the rain tap against a skylight above you.

Bringing the Oasis Home

A small bathroom shouldn't limit your design aspirations. By trading a bulky tub for a sleek, curbless walk-in shower, prioritizing natural PNW textures, and keeping sightlines open with clear glass, you can create a bathroom that feels incredibly spacious, functional, and deeply rooted in Northwest style.

item.title: Case Study: Master Bedroom & Bedroom Window Upgrades in Redmond, WA
item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com
item.content:encoded:
When it comes to boosting a home's energy efficiency, curbing exterior noise, and elevating curb appeal, replacing old windows is one of the smartest investments a homeowner can make.

We recently completed a comprehensive window replacement and exterior trim upgrade project for a beautiful home in Redmond, Washington. By swapping out aged vinyl inserts with high-performance, sound-controlled custom windows, we dramatically improved both the interior comfort and exterior styling of the property.

Here is a look behind the scenes at how our team executed this project from initial measurements to final trim.

The Project Specifications

For this home, the focus was on updating windows across the upper levels, specifically targeting the Master Bedroom and an adjacent bedroom. Because the home sits in an active neighborhood, acoustic insulation was a top priority alongside thermal efficiency.

  • Window Type: High-quality vinyl window units with an elegant white-on-white interior and exterior finish.

  • Glass Technology: SunCoat® Low-E glass coupled with Sound Control (STC) and tempered safety glass. This setup maximizes UV protection, retains indoor climate control, and significantly dampens outdoor ambient noise.

  • Installation Method: Premium pocket/insert installation using a standard 1-3/8" setback nail fin.

Step-by-Step Execution

1. Precision Diagnostic Measurements

Every successful window installation starts with accurate paperwork. Our project technician carefully mapped out the net width and height configurations for each opening.

The Master Bedroom units required a generous 71½" x 59½" frame footprint , while the secondary bedroom called for a 71½" x 47½" sizing. We utilized structural tape measures to verify existing frame plumb, level, and square metrics before ordering the custom vinyl packages.

2. Siding Cutback & Exterior Prep

With the new custom windows safely on-site, the physical transformation began on the home's exterior.

  • First, our team removed the original surface-mounted exterior trim pieces.

  • Because this home features durable Hardie Lap siding, we used an angle grinder to precisely cut back the siding and liner around the window openings. This clean cutback is necessary to expose the underlying wood framing studs so the new window's integrated nailing fin can mount directly to the house structure.

3. Weatherproofing with Advanced Flashing

In the Pacific Northwest, robust moisture protection is non-negotiable. Once the raw framing was exposed, we wrapped the window perimeters tightly with Fortiflash Waterproof Flashing Membrane. This self-adhesive flashing creates an impenetrable barrier against wind-driven rain and moisture migration, ensuring the wall cavity stays dry for decades to come.

4. Setting the Windows & Custom Timber Trim

With the openings fully protected, the new vinyl units were set in place, perfectly leveled, and fastened via their nail fins.

To give the exterior an upscale, intentional architectural look, we ditched standard narrow trim molding. Instead, we custom-fabricated a heavy-duty trim package using Primed Finger-Joint (PFJ) Cedar:

  • Top & Bottom Header/Sill: $5/4 \times 8$ PFJ Cedar featuring an elegant 1-inch overhang beyond the legs.

  • Side Legs: Matching $5/4 \times 6$ PFJ Cedar casing.

The entire assembly was meticulously sealed with high-grade white exterior sealant to keep water out and lock a clean, contrasting aesthetic in place.

The Finished Result

The results speak for themselves! From the inside, the new multi-lite casement and picture window configurations flood the bedrooms with beautiful natural light while sealing out drafts and street noise.

From the exterior, the crisp white vinyl frames framed by the substantial, blue-primed shadow-line cedar trim completely revitalize the back facade of the home. The home is now more energy-efficient, significantly quieter, and ready to face whatever weather Washington throws its way.

Planning a window or door upgrade for your home? Contact our team today to schedule your own precision diagnostic consultation!

item.title: Bringing Light in While Keeping Views Out: A Guide to Andersen's Obscure Glass Options for Seattle Homeowners
item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com
item.content:encoded:
Bringing Light in While Keeping Views Out: A Guide to Andersen's Obscure Glass Options for Seattle Homeowners

Living in the Seattle area means we have a unique relationship with natural light. When the sun breaks through the gray, or during those long, glorious Pacific Northwest summer days, we want every ounce of daylight flooding into our homes. At the same time, with homes nestled close together in neighborhoods from Queen Anne to West Seattle, privacy is a major priority.

So how do you maximize precious natural light without giving your neighbors a front-row seat to your daily life?

You don’t have to resort to heavy, dust-catching blinds that block out the sun. Andersen Windows & Doors offers a stunning lineup of specialty privacy-patterned glass options that obscure visibility while letting beautiful, diffused light pour into your home.

If you look at the Additional Glass Options Info Sheet below, you can see exactly how these unique textures distort the view of an object (like a vibrant red vase) while keeping the space feeling open, bright, and private.

Click the link below

additional-glass-options-info-sheet

Here is how you can use Andersen's obscure glass styles to elevate your Seattle home design.

The Andersen Obscure Glass Lineup

Andersen provides several distinct patterned glass textures, each offering a different visual aesthetic and level of privacy to fit your home's architectural style—whether it's a historic Craftsman or a sleek, modern new build:

1. Satin Etch Glass

Satin Etch is a favorite for contemporary Pacific Northwest architecture. It is a pearlescent glass that offers a smooth, frosted, and highly sophisticated look. It delivers a high level of privacy by thoroughly obscuring shapes, yet it allows light to share beautifully between spaces. It’s perfect for creating clean, minimalist bathroom windows or modern entryways that let in the morning light without sacrificing security.

2. Cascade Glass

Perfect for our rain-loving region, Cascade glass mimics the organic look of falling water or rain running down a surface. This textured glass adds an elegant, dynamic movement to your windows. Best of all, it can be ordered in either a vertical or horizontal orientation, letting you customize how the "water" flows across your design.

3. Reed Glass

Characterized by clean, distinct parallel lines, Reed glass (often called English Reed) offers a brilliant geometric distortion. It catches the light dramatically, making it a spectacular choice for transitional homes and modern townhouses alike. Like Cascade, Andersen allows you to specify a vertical or horizontal pattern layout depending on your home's aesthetic.

4. Fern Glass

If you love a more traditional, nature-inspired, or artistic flair, Fern glass (also known as Single Glue Chip) features an elegant, textured frost that looks like delicate ice crystals or organic fern fronds blooming across the glass. It breaks up the light beautifully while keeping the view completely private—fitting in flawlessly with classic Seattle homes.

5. Obscure Glass

Often referred to as standard patterned obscure glass (or Stippolyte), this option features a classic, tightly pebbled texture. It provides a timeless, uniform distortion that works incredibly well in utilitarian spaces like walk-in showers, powder rooms, or side-entry garage doors.

6. Spraylite

As captured in the "image001 (6).jpg" breakdown, Spraylite glass features a softer, water-droplet or subtle stucco-like texture. It provides a unique, gentle distortion that sits comfortably between standard obscure glass and the high-movement patterns like Cascade.

Modern Customization: Glass Spacers for the PNW Aesthetic

Privacy glass isn't the only way Andersen lets you customize your view. To achieve that crisp, high-end look popular in Seattle modern architecture, Andersen also offers premium Glass Spacer Options.

The glass spacer is the small bar that separates the panes of glass in your window. While standard windows use stainless steel, Andersen lets you choose between Black and White glass spacers to perfectly match your design intent:

  • Sleek & Modern: Black spacers create a crisp "shadow line" that complements dark window frames (like black or dark bronze) beautifully.

  • Bright & Clean: White spacers blend seamlessly into lighter frames for an uninterrupted look.

  • Perfect Match: If you add Full Divided Light grilles to your windows, the internal grille spacer bar will perfectly match your chosen spacer color (Black or White), creating a flawless, cohesive finish.

Where to Use Obscure Glass in Your Seattle Home

While you can put privacy glass anywhere you want to soften the sunlight or obscure an unsightly view (like a neighboring house that sits just a few feet away), here are the most common applications for local homes:

  • The Primary Bathroom: Use Satin Etch or Obscure glass by the bathtub or in the shower enclosure. You'll get to enjoy natural morning light on those gray winter days without needing heavy window blinds.

  • Front Entryways & Transoms: Bring light into a dark foyer using Reed or Cascade glass flanking your front door. It keeps your entryway bright while ensuring delivery drivers or visitors on the porch can’t look inside.

  • Daylight Basements & Home Offices: If your office or bonus room faces a busy street, sidewalk, or alleyway, obscure glass filters out visual distractions so you can focus, all while keeping your workspace naturally lit.

Series Availability

Andersen makes it incredibly easy to bring these privacy options to life across their product spectrum. Popular lines like the E-Series, A-Series, 400 Series, 100 Series, and various MultiGlide or Folding doors all support the Satin Etch glass and premium black spacer customizations.

Ready to swap out those dusty blinds for a sleek, permanently private view that embraces every bit of daylight? Check out the pattern chart in  and contact your local Seattle-area Andersen dealer today to see these beautiful glass samples in person!

item.title: How to Measure Window Glass for a Replacement (Without Replacing the Whole Frame!)
item.dc:creator: dan@soundviewseattle.com
item.content:encoded:
Replacing a broken or foggy window pane doesn't mean you need to tear out the whole window and spend a small fortune on a full unit replacement. If your frame is still sturdy, opting for a glass-only replacement (whether for a picture window or double-hung sash) saves serious money and time.

The secret to a seamless DIY fix comes down to getting your tape measure out and taking accurate dimensions. Here is how to measure your window glass like a pro before ordering your replacement pane.

Step-by-Step Measuring Instructions

1. Measure the Width Hold your tape measure horizontally and record the distance between the inner edges of the vinyl or wood stops that secure the glass inside the frame.

2. Measure the Height Run your tape measure vertically between the inner edges of the vinyl or wood stops holding the glass in place.

Pro-Tips to Avoid Pricey Mistakes

  • Measure where the glass sits: Always focus on the edge-to-edge area inside the frame where the glass actually rests.

  • Ignore the outer trim: Do NOT measure the exterior window frame or decorative trim surrounding the window. Including the trim will result in ordering a pane that is far too large to fit into your sash.

Ready to get your window back in top shape? Grab your measurements and contact us today to order your custom-cut replacement glass!
